name: State-Space Momentum Regime (SSMR)
concept: Detects hidden momentum regimes using a Kalman filter on price and volume state vectors.
instructions: Compute a 2‑dimensional state vector [price, volume] and run a Kalman filter with a constant‑velocity model; extract the filtered velocity as momentum and the filter covariance trace as regime confidence; generate a long signal when velocity > 0 and confidence < 0.5 inside London‑NY killzone, short when velocity < 0 and confidence < 0.5; ensure first‑bar trigger only.

name: Fractal Dimension Trend Divergence (FDTD)
concept: Uses rolling fractal dimension to separate trending from ranging markets and aligns with order‑block retests.
instructions: Calculate the Higuchi fractal dimension on the close series over a 50‑bar window; label bars with dimension < 1.2 as ranging and > 1.4 as trending; when trending and price revisits the most recent bullish order block (identified via find_swings) generate a long, opposite for bearish; apply ADX > 25 filter and killzone gating; use one‑time entry logic.

name: Spectral Density Breakout (SDB)
concept: Identifies low‑frequency power spikes in the price spectrum as precursors to large breakouts.
instructions: Apply a Fast Fourier Transform on the last 256 close values; compute power spectral density and sum power below the 0.05 Hz band; when this low‑frequency power exceeds its 30‑bar rolling mean by 2 σ, and price breaks above the Donchian upper channel, trigger a long; reverse for short when power drops and price breaks below lower channel; restrict to NY session.

name: Regime‑Switching Volatility Clustering (RSVC)
concept: A hidden Markov model classifies volatility regimes and only trades in low‑volatility clusters awaiting volatility expansion.
instructions: Fit a 2‑state Gaussian HMM on the 14‑period ATR series using the hmmlearn library (states: low‑vol, high‑vol); label current state; when in low‑vol state and a bullish FVG appears, open long; when in low‑vol and bearish FVG, open short; require rvol > 1.3 and killzone filter; ensure single‑bar entry.

name: Multiscale Wavelet Decomposition Trend (MWDT)
concept: Decomposes price into wavelet scales to isolate the dominant trend component for signal generation.
instructions: Perform a discrete wavelet transform (Daubechies 4) on the last 128 close values; reconstruct the approximation at level 3 as the trend line; compute its slope over the last 8 bars; if slope > 0 and price is above the trend line, generate long; if slope < 0 and price below trend line, generate short; filter with efficiency_ratio > 0.3 and London killzone.

name: Dynamic Correlation with EUR‑GBP (DC‑EGBP)
concept: Exploits temporary divergence between EURUSD and EURGBP to capture cross‑currency arbitrage.
instructions: Fetch synchronized EURGBP 5‑min close series; compute rolling 30‑bar Pearson correlation; when correlation drops below 0.4 and EURUSD closes above its VWAP while EURGBP is below its VWAP, go long EURUSD; opposite condition for short; require ADX > 20 and NY‑London overlap; one‑time entry per divergence event.

name: Entropy‑Based Liquidity Imbalance (EBLI)
concept: Measures information entropy of bid‑ask volume distribution to spot institutional liquidity sweeps.
instructions: Approximate bid‑ask volume by splitting total volume into upper and lower halves of the candle range; compute Shannon entropy over a 20‑bar window; when entropy falls below its 20‑bar rolling median indicating concentrated liquidity and a BSL sweep occurs, trigger short; when entropy low and SSL sweep, trigger long; enforce killzone and risk rules.

name: Non‑Linear Phase Space Rotation (NLPSR)
concept: Maps price‑volume pairs into a phase‑space and detects rotational patterns indicative of accumulation or distribution.
instructions: Create a 2‑D trajectory of normalized price change and volume change over the last 30 bars; compute the signed area (cross product) of the polygon; positive area signals clockwise rotation (accumulation) → long, negative → short; require rvol > 1.2 and ADX > 22; limit to London‑NY session and first‑bar trigger.

name: Adaptive Fractal‑Based Stop Engine (AFSE)
concept: Derives stop‑loss levels from the local fractal dimension to adapt to market roughness.
instructions: Calculate rolling Higuchi dimension over 40 bars; set sl_long = close - (1.5 * atr(14) * (1 + (fd - 1.2))) and sl_short = close + (1.5 * atr(14) * (1 + (fd - 1.2))); generate entry when price breaks recent bullish order block and fd > 1.4 for long, fd < 1.2 for short; apply killzone and momentum filters; ensure risk distance >= 2.5.

name: Spectral Ratio Momentum (SRM)
concept: Compares high‑frequency to low‑frequency power ratios to gauge short‑term momentum bursts.
instructions: Compute FFT on last 128 closes; sum power in 0.2‑0.5 Hz band (high) and 0.01‑0.05 Hz band (low); calculate ratio = high/low; when ratio exceeds its 30‑bar rolling mean by 1.5 σ and price is above VWAP, go long; opposite for short; require rvol > 1.3, ADX > 25, and NY killzone.

name: Markov Transition Liquidity Grid (MTLG)
concept: Builds a Markov transition matrix of price moves between discrete liquidity zones to predict next‑move bias.
instructions: Define three zones: below swing low, between swing low/high, above swing high; count transitions over last 200 bars to form a 3×3 matrix; compute probability of moving up from current zone; if up‑prob > 0.6 and a bullish FVG appears, trigger long; if down‑prob > 0.6 and bearish FVG, trigger short; filter with efficiency_ratio > 0.28 and London session.

name: Recursive Kalman‑Enhanced Supertrend (RK‑ST)
concept: Feeds Kalman‑filtered price into Supertrend to obtain a smoother trend line with reduced noise.
instructions: Apply Kalman filter to close series (constant‑acceleration model) and obtain filtered price; run supertrend on filtered price with period 10, mult 3; generate long when direction = 1 and price > filtered VWAP, short when direction = -1 and price < filtered VWAP; require ADX > 22 and rvol > 1.2; enforce first‑bar entry inside London‑NY killzone.

name: Fractal‑Weighted Order Block (FWOB)
concept: Weights order‑block strength by local fractal dimension to prioritize high‑confidence zones.
instructions: Identify bullish and bearish order blocks via find_swings; compute fractal dimension over 30 bars surrounding each block; assign weight = fd; trigger long when a bullish block with weight > 1.5 is retested and price closes above block; short for bearish block with weight > 1.5; apply rvol > 1.25, ADX > 20, and killzone filter.

name: Cross‑Asset Spectral Correlation (CASC)
concept: Uses spectral correlation between EURUSD and US10Y Treasury futures to capture macro‑driven moves.
instructions: Obtain synchronized US10Y close series; compute FFT on both series over 256 bars; calculate cosine similarity of their low‑frequency spectra; when similarity drops below 0.3 and EURUSD breaks above its daily pivot R1, go long; opposite for short when similarity low and price breaks below S1; require ADX > 25, rvol > 1.3, and NY session.

name: Regime‑Adaptive Risk Scaling (RARS)
concept: Adjusts stop‑loss and take‑profit distances dynamically based on detected volatility regime via GARCH.
instructions: Fit a rolling GARCH(1,1) model on 14‑period returns to estimate conditional volatility; if volatility > rolling median, set sl_long = low - (2.0 * cond_vol) and tp_long = close + (3.0 * (close - sl_long)); if volatility <= median, use 1.5 * cond_vol for SL and 2.0 R for TP; generate entry on bullish FVG with ADX > 22 and London‑NY killzone; ensure risk distance >= 2.5 and first‑bar trigger.
